messages:
Ana: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-routing rollout we see a pretty consistent drop in prefix cache hit rate for streaming chat requests. Hit rate went from ~82% -> ~56% on the 2.7B family during peak.
Mike: Ugh. Is that the new kernel-selection heuristic that picks an fp16-friendly kernel for short sequences?
Ana: Yeah. We routed by 'fastest-estimate' instead of model+quantization tag. Probable cause: the kernel chooser is selecting different execution paths for requests that used to map to the same cache key, invalidating prefix/kv cache locality.
Sasha: Can you paste the profiler output you saw? :eyes:
Ana: Sure — abridged profiling (per-request tail) from the warm run:
```
p50 latency: 38ms  p95: 123ms  p99: 310ms
kv_prefetch_misses: +34%  prefix_cache_hits: 56% (was 82%)
batch_compose_size_avg: 6.2 -> 4.1  max_queue_ms: 12
kernel_switches_per_request: 1.9 -> 2.7
```
Kevin: The average batch size dropping is concerning — continuous batcher probably mixing shorter/longer sequences more aggressively because kernels changed execution time estimates.
Lina: Did we change keying anywhere? The cache key should include model_id + quant_tag + prefix_hash. If quant_tag is omitted on the new path, keys won't match.
Ana: We confirmed keying code is intact in the cache layer. The quant_tag is present in the key for cached entries. The difference seems to be that kernel selection inserts a transient path that bypasses the prefix-lookup in some code paths when a 'fast' kernel is chosen for streaming micro-batches.
Mike: That implies two problems: 1) reduced prefix reuse due to batch composition changing, 2) some requests skipping prefix lookup entirely (bug). Which is it?
Ana: Looks like both. The skip is a bug: a fast-path for minimal context was added and forgot to call into prefix_cache.lookup when continuous batching flagged "immediate_dequeue=true".
Sasha: Repro script (small):
```
# reproduce: streaming load with mixed prompt lengths
loadtest --model redwood-2.7b --streams 200 --mix "short:60%,long:40%" --max_wait_ms 10
```
Lina: For the batching side, if the batcher now groups more heterogeneously because kernel_time estimates changed, hit-rate drops even though cache keys are stable. We should try making batch composition prefer same-prefix cohorts (sticky-batching).
Kevin: Agreed. Sticky-batching heuristic: when a new request arrives, if there is an existing pending batch with matching prefix hash (or same recent model+quant tag) and age < N ms, add to that batch, otherwise start a new one. Keep N small (5-20ms) to avoid latency regression.
Mike: Also need a quick fix for the bug where prefix lookup is skipped. Ana — can you open a tiny PR to always call prefix_cache.lookup before taking any fast-path?
Ana: On it. Drafting PR now. Will add a regression test that runs the reproduce script and asserts prefix_cache_hits > 75% on the baseline config.
perf-bot: Perf test queued — job id 8492. Will run against canary and baseline.
Sasha: In parallel, let's instrument kernel_selector decisions in logs: emit which kernel id and selection reason per request (sampler/estimate/fallback). That will help us correlate kernel choices to cache hits.
Lina: We should also try two experiments:
- Experiment A (conservative): disable 'fastest-estimate' routing for streaming workloads — go back to model+quant pinned kernels.
- Experiment B (cohorting): enable sticky-batching + prefer matching prefix_hash groups for continuous batcher.
Kevin: Measure both for: prefix_cache_hit_rate, avg batch_size, p95 latency, token throughput, and cost-per-token delta.
Ana: I'll run A first as a rollback canary. If that restores hit rate and p95 within 10% of baseline, we keep model-pinned routing for streaming while we refine selector heuristics.
Mike: Timeline?
Ana: PR for the lookup bug in next 30m. Canary for Experiment A by EOD if perf-bot jobs are green. Experiment B will take an engineering day to wire into the batcher and add tunables (sticky window ms, cohort-key size). I'll draft RFC in #eng-runtime after we have pilot numbers.
Sasha: Add a dashboard card with a small scatter: kernel_id vs prefix_hit_rate (1h rollup). Quick visual will surface misbehaving kernels.
perf-bot: Job 8492 completed: canary vs baseline diff: prefix_hit_rate dropped -26pp on canary, p95 +34% (detailed logs in CI).
Ana: Ok that's consistent. Rolling kernel routing change back for streaming by toggling route policy flag. I'll also attach the small e2e test to the gating checks.
Mike: Thanks — let's sync in 30 to review the PR and perf plots. :thumbsup:
Lina: One extra thought — keying could also include selected_kernel_signature as part of key when kernels are intentionally non-functional-equivalent (rare). But do that only if kernel determinism isn't guaranteed.
Kevin: Good note. For now, ensure the cache lookup is always hit and batch composition is tuned. Long-term we can discuss kernel-stable keys.
Ana: Filing action items in the thread and will follow up with links to PR/CI. Thanks all.
